title: Band gaps and light emission
summary: Semiconductors by family and band structure: whether the band gap is direct decides whether a material can emit light efficiently.

concepts.label: Semiconductor
concepts.description: A material with a band gap between its filled valence band and its empty conduction band; here a stable element or binary compound.

children.label: Semiconductor family
children.description: Groups of the constituent elements: IV (Si), III-V (GaAs), II-VI (ZnSe), I-VII (CuBr).

children.label: Crystal structure
children.description: Space group of the ground state: 227 diamond, 216 zincblende, 186 wurtzite, 225 rocksalt.

children.label: Electronegativity difference
children.description: Pauling χ difference of the two elements: a measure of how ionic the bond is.

concepts.label: Band gap
concepts.description: Energy between the valence-band maximum and the conduction-band minimum, eV.

children.label: Direct band gap
children.description: Both band edges at the same crystal momentum: a photon alone can be absorbed or emitted.

children.label: Indirect band gap
children.description: Band edges at different momenta: recombination needs a phonon, so emission is weak (Si, Ge, AlAs, GaP).

children.label: Band-gap problem of DFT
children.description: Semi-local functionals such as PBE underestimate gaps, often by 30–100%; hybrid functionals or GW come closer.

facts.text: Alexandria's gaps are PBE; measured Si is 1.12 eV, GaAs 1.42 eV at 300 K.

children.label: Measured band gap
children.description: Experimental gap from optical absorption or photoluminescence.

concepts.label: Light-emitting diode
concepts.description: A p-n junction that emits photons at about the band-gap energy, λ ≈ 1240 nm·eV / E_g.

children.label: Radiative recombination
children.description: An electron falling across the gap and emitting a photon; fast in direct-gap materials.
